## The contract (pinned; B is coding against this verbatim)

src/calc.js is an ES module. It must ALSO be valid as a classic <script> once the build step strips the leading `export ` keyword from each export line — so: no `import`, no top-level await, only `export const/function` at column 0, and everything else plain.

```
export const DEFAULTS = {
  // one entry per key in assumptions.md sections 1–5 and 7 (numbers only; string-valued rows like concrete_grade_structural and rooms_are_all_spaces go in ASSUMPTION_NOTES below)
  key: { value: number, unit: string, label: string /* plain English */, group: 'blocks'|'walls'|'concrete'|'steel'|'prices'|'wastage', rationale: string, source: string, sourceUrl: string|null, confidence: 'Certain'|'Likely'|'Guessing', lastChecked: 'YYYY-MM-DD' },
  ...
};
export const ASSUMPTION_NOTES = [ { key, value: string, rationale, source, confidence, lastChecked } ];  // concrete_grade_structural, rooms_are_all_spaces, construction_system
export const LIMITS = { floors: [1, 4], wallHeightM: [2.4, 4.5], roomSideM: [1, 20], rooms: [1, 40], areaM2: [30, 1500] };
export const SAMPLE_HOUSE = { floors: 2, wallHeightM: 3.0, rooms: [ /* ALL spaces of one ~200 m² floor: majlis, living, dining, kitchen, 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, hall/corridor, store — name, lengthM, widthM — summing to 195–205 m² */ ] };
export function generateRooms(areaM2) → rooms[]   // the m² shortcut: a plausible full set of spaces (same kinds as SAMPLE_HOUSE, scaled) whose areas sum to areaM2 within ±2%; deterministic; throws plain-English Error if areaM2 outside LIMITS.areaM2
export function validateHouse(house) → house      // throws Error with a plain-English message (name the field and the allowed range) on: non-object, floors/wallHeightM/room sides not finite or outside LIMITS, empty rooms, missing/blank room name (default to "Room N" instead of throwing)
export function estimate(house, overrides = {}) → result
```

  assumptionsUsed: [ { key, label, value, unit, defaultValue, overridden: boolean, source, sourceUrl, confidence, lastChecked } ],  // every DEFAULTS key, in DEFAULTS order
  notes: [ string ]  // plain-English caveats: prices are editable defaults not quotes; excludes mortar/finishes/MEP/labour; which prices are "Guessing"
}

All quantities in the result are numbers already including wastage (wastage per MATERIAL: block_wastage_pct, concrete_wastage_pct, rebar_wastage_pct — each element row reports the pct that applied to it). Blocks are whole numbers (Math.ceil). Costs use the price keys; external blocks at price_omr_block_200, internal at price_omr_block_150, concrete at price_omr_readymix_c30_m3, steel at price_omr_rebar_tonne. Never return NaN or Infinity anywhere — validate first.

Geometry (from assumptions.md): floorAreaM2 = Σ room areas; builtUpAreaM2 = floorAreaM2 × floors; extWallLengthM = ext_perimeter_shape_factor × 4 × √floorAreaM2; intWallLengthM = int_wall_per_room_factor × Σ(L+W); wall areas = length × wallHeightM × floors, then × (1 − opening_deduction_pct/100); blocks = net area × blocks_per_m2_wall × (1 + wastage). ## Tests (test/calc.test.mjs, node:test + node:assert, run with `node --test test/`)
- DEFAULTS: every entry has all fields, numeric value, a lastChecked date, a confidence from the allowed set; every key in assumptions.md's tables (grep the file in the test, parse the `| key |` rows) exists in DEFAULTS or ASSUMPTION_NOTES, and vice versa.

report:
Builder A done. Two files written, nothing else touched.

Files
- src/calc.js — DEFAULTS (30 numeric rows, sections 1–5 + 7, each with label, group, rationale, source, sourceUrl, confidence, lastChecked), ASSUMPTION_NOTES (construction_system, concrete_grade_structural, rooms_are_all_spaces), LIMITS, SAMPLE_HOUSE, generateRooms, validateHouse, estimate — exactly the pinned contract shape. Every formula has a comment naming the assumption keys it uses. No imports, no template literals, only `export const/function` at column 0.
- test/calc.test.mjs — 20 tests, node:test.

Sample house headline totals (golden snapshot, pinned in the test)
14 spaces, 204.9 m²/floor, 2 floors → 8,053 blocks (4,408 external + 3,645 internal), 129.08 m³ concrete, 12.909 t steel; cost 1,794.55 (blocks) + 4,130.56 (concrete) + 3,356.26 (steel) = 9,281.37 OMR.

Tests: 20 tests, 20 pass, 0 fail. The classic-script proof (`export ` stripped, run through `new Function`) produced byte-identical totals.

Interpretations I had to make (reviewer, please check these three)
1. Ground-slab steel. The contract's type sketch shows groundSlab.steelKg: 0 but allows judgment. I apply rebar_kg_per_m3_slabs to the ground slab, because assumptions.md section 6 spreads steel over ALL concrete including it — with zero, the sample falls to 10.9 t, below section 7's 11–16 t range. Documented in a code comment.
2. Sample house size. Section 7's floor of 8,000 blocks is only just reachable inside the 195–205 m² window: my sample lands at 204.9 m² and 8,053 blocks. The margin is ~0.7% — honest arithmetic, not tuned numbers, but a small future change to the shape factor or opening deduction could push the sample under the assertion.
3. Wastage per row. Concrete rows report concrete_wastage_pct; wall rows report block_wastage_pct. Steel inside a concrete row uses rebar_wastage_pct, which the row cannot display in a single field — the results notes state all three percentages instead.
Also: ext_wall_perimeter_factor (section 2) is superseded by ext_perimeter_shape_factor (section 7) for the external-wall formula; it stays in DEFAULTS with its rationale saying so. Cement, sand and aggregate prices are carried for traceability but not used in v1 costs (mortar is out of scope).

One thing for the lead, not a code fault: the verify recipe's step 1, `node --test test/`, FAILS on this Node 22.22 build (a directory argument is resolved as a module). `node --test test/*.mjs` runs the suite fine. CONVENTIONS.md is outside my two files, so I did not edit it.

Orchestrator: recipe step 1 changed to `node --test test/*.mjs` in CONVENTIONS.md. The three interpretations go to code-reviewer as explicit checks.
